steps.title: تَ, added to a pattern you already know
body: Form V's signature is تَ prefixed to Form II's own pattern, giving the shape تَفَعَّلَ — the doubled middle consonant from Form II is still there, just with تَ added in front.
تَكَلَّمَ ("to speak"), already in your vocabulary since A1, is a Form V verb: تَكَلَّمَ, present tense يَتَكَلَّمُ.

Form V is most often the reflexive of Form II — doing, or becoming the target of, Form II's action yourself. تَكَلَّمَ has no attested Form II "كَلَّمَ" used the same way in everyday MSA; the pattern's tendency still holds even when the "paired" form isn't itself a common word.

steps.title: Form V in one sentence
steps.intro: Read the sentence, then check what marks it as Form V. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: تَكَلَّمَ starts with تَ and still has a doubled middle letter underneath. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: تَفَعَّلَ is تَ added to Form II's own doubled-consonant pattern — the mark of Form V. Form VI instead adds تَ to Form III's long-alif pattern.

steps.title: Meaning tendencies
steps.prompt: تَكَلَّمَ is Form V — تَ added to Form II's own pattern. What does Form V often mean?

options.label: The reflexive of Form II — doing (or becoming) that action to/for yourself
Seeking or considering something to be true
A color or a physical defect

steps.explanation: Form V's تَ prefix is the same reflexive تَ you'll see again on Form VI — Form V takes Form II's causative/intensive sense and turns it back on the subject.

steps.title: Halfway there
steps.message: Form V — تَ + Form II's pattern, often reflexive. Four forms down, four to go.
